issues.failure_explanation: The introduction claims O(h^2+tau^2) convergence for the fully-discrete Crank-Nicolson scheme and O(h^2) convergence regardless of theta. Theorem thm:convergence-theta proves O(h^2+tau^2) only under the additional hypothesis that T is an integral multiple of tau. Without this condition the proven rate is O(h^2+tau). With the algorithm's choice tau = h for theta = 1/2 and T not a multiple of h, the achieved rate is O(h^2+h) = O(h), not O(h^2).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify both the O(h^2+tau^2) Crank-Nicolson claim and the O(h^2) uniform-in-theta claim in the introduction by adding the condition that T is an integral multiple of tau (or equivalently that tau divides T).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised O(h^2+tau^2) Crank-Nicolson convergence rate and the O(h^2) rate for all theta are not established for general T; they hold only when T is an integral multiple of tau (for theta = 1/2).
issues.title: Prose overclaims O(h^2+tau^2) Crank-Nicolson convergence without the T-multiple-of-tau condition
issues.why_classification: Adding a single condition to two prose sentences preserves every formal result and guarantee. The condition is routinely ensured in practice by choosing tau = T/n. No new argument or construction is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\left\|U-\Pi_h(u(T))_{i,j}\right\|_{\ell_h^2}\leq C_{T,u_0,f,\gamma,\zeta} (h^2+\tau),
\text{where } U \text{ is the output vector of Algorithm \ref{alg:theta-heat-hyperbolic}}.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm's Repeat loop with condition k*tau > T (strict inequality) outputs U at step floor(T/tau)+1, i.e., at time exceeding T by up to tau. For T = n*tau, the output is U^{n+1} at time T+tau. The proof of the 'Moreover' clause bounds ||E^{k_{tau,T}}|| = ||U^n - Pi_h u(T)|| <= C(h^2+tau^2), but the theorem's claimed quantity is ||U^{n+1} - Pi_h u(T)||, which includes the additional time-shift error ||Pi_h u((n+1)tau) - Pi_h u(n*tau)|| = O(tau). Hence the actual error is O(h^2+tau^2) + O(tau) = O(h^2+tau), not O(h^2+tau^2).

failure_location.quote: Moreover, if $\theta=\frac{1}{2}$ (i.e., when we use the Crank-Nicolson scheme) and $T$ is an integral multiple of $\tau$, then the order of the convergence above is $\mathcal{O}(h^2+\tau^2)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the loop condition in Algorithm alg:theta-heat-hyperbolic from 'k tau > T' to 'k tau >= T' so that the output is U^{floor(T/tau)}, matching the quantity bounded in the proof. This restores the O(h^2+tau^2) rate when T is an integral multiple of tau.
issues.overall_effect: The O(h^2+tau^2) Crank-Nicolson convergence guarantee in Theorem thm:convergence-theta is false for the algorithm as written, even when T is an integral multiple of tau. With the algorithm's choice tau = h, the achieved rate is O(h) rather than the advertised O(h^2).
issues.title: Algorithm loop condition causes one-step discrepancy making the O(h^2+tau^2) Crank-Nicolson guarantee false
issues.why_classification: A one-character change to the loop inequality (>= replacing >) makes the algorithm's output coincide with the quantity bounded in the proof, preserving every substantive claim and guarantee. No new argument or construction is needed.
